llm_proposer.assessment: The most likely cause is an ODU cross-connect misconfiguration on svc375's active path. The simultaneous bidirectional ODU_TIM and CLIENT_SF alarms, while every neighboring service and optical measurement remains normal, isolate the problem to svc375's ODU switching rather than the shared optical line.

proposals.rationale: An incorrect cross-connect can deliver only svc375 to the wrong ODU destination, directly explaining ODU_TIM and consequent CLIENT_SF at both endpoints without any optical PM change. The exact switch site is not identified, and a single-direction misconnect would not by itself explain the symmetric alarms.

A failed endpoint client port could interrupt svc375 while leaving all other services and optical paths healthy. It is unlikely because one local client-port failure does not naturally produce simultaneous ODU_TIM at both endpoints.

A switch-fabric problem on the ODU path could interrupt the service without changing optical telemetry. A full OTN switch failure should disrupt every ODU crossing that switch, which is strongly contradicted by the many unaffected neighboring services.
